A 7.1% weekly gain with roughly $460M Friday turnover followed Q4 revenue growth of 5.4%, stronger free cash flow and FY27 guidance; the bullish technical trend is compelling but fundamental and macro signals remain mixed.

An 11.0% weekly advance and roughly $522M Friday turnover followed Q3 sales growth and higher full-year sales and EPS guidance, while StockLens identifies leading relative strength within medical devices.
An 8.5% weekly gain with about $538M Friday turnover followed Q1 FY27 revenue growth of 5%, adjusted EPS growth of 28% and raised FY27 EPS guidance; macro sensitivity remains the main risk.
A 14.2% weekly advance followed FY27 Q1 revenue growth of 11%, adjusted EPS growth of 32% and raised full-year outlook; momentum is strong but the earnings gap calls for a pullback or consolidation.
A 7.5% weekly gain follows Q3 sales growth and an improved 2026 outlook, while current StockLens fundamentals and risk posture are supportive; insider selling and consumer caution temper conviction.
A 3.9% weekly advance and 1.2M Friday shares traded followed higher FY26 FFO guidance and a dividend increase, with real-estate relative strength improving; rate sensitivity remains material.

A 2.2% weekly gain and roughly $3.9B Friday dollar turnover accompany FY26 Q4 revenue growth of 13%, payment-volume growth of 9% and adjusted EPS growth of 17%; low relative volatility supports a liquid continuation setup, though insider selling is a caution.

A 1.6% weekly advance and roughly $298M Friday turnover show resilience against a falling broad market, while StockLens reports a very strong bullish trend and healthy cash-flow profile; utility-sector weakness limits upside.

A 2.4% weekly advance and roughly $1.3B Friday turnover show defensive relative strength with a bullish technical trend and solid balance sheet; broad insider selling and input-cost pressure remain important cautions.

A 2.1% weekly gain while XLK fell about 8.2%, alongside Q3 organic revenue growth and higher FY26 guidance, shows unusual relative resilience; the very strong trend is extended and technology macro remains a headwind.

sector_notes: Communication services, consumer discretionary, financials and real estate showed the best weekly relative strength, while technology—especially semiconductors—and energy were the clearest breakdowns: XLK fell about 8.2%, SOXX 13.1% and XLE 12.0%, versus SPY down 2.7% and QQQ down 5.0%. Friday's rebound in the Nasdaq and semiconductors followed a severe Thursday selloff, but the fourth consecutive weekly Nasdaq decline and elevated volatility argue for selective, catalyst-backed swings rather than broad AI-beta exposure. October payrolls beat expectations and unemployment fell to 4.1%, increasing rate sensitivity ahead of US CPI on November 10 and PPI on November 13.
